clue.text: German girl backed emperor in Eastern city

indicators.note: backed means turned round, so the girl's name is read from its end

parts.note: Irma is a girl's name of German origin
a tsar was the emperor of Russia

explanation.surface: A German girl supports an emperor somewhere in an Eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns IRMA into AMRI; 'in' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Amritsar is a city in the Punjab, northern India, home of the Golden Temple.

clue.text: Ma and Pa upset with clue? It's my fault!

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Mum and Dad, upset by a crossword clue, admit the mistake was theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of MAPACLUE, signalled by 'upset', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mea culpa is Latin for through my fault, an admission of guilt.

clue.text: Exercise equipment for team in 1 or 24, say

parts.note: the answers to 1 across and 24 down are both cities in India, so things there are of that country
a club is a sports team

explanation.surface: Gym kit for a team based in one of two cities.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR read '1' as 'I'. Indian clubs are bottle-shaped wooden clubs swung in exercise routines.
explanation.definitionFit: Indian clubs are juggling-pin shaped weights swung for exercise.

clue.text: "Sheer" ought to provide alternative for this

definitions.text: "Sheer" ought to provide alternative for this

indicators.note: providing an alternative means offering a different arrangement of the same letters

explanation.surface: The word sheer should be able to stand in for this word.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging SHEER OUGHT gives the answer, and sheer fabric is exactly what the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer fabric is thin enough to be transparent, letting light and sight pass.

clue.text: Appropriately, give back note fairly

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
fairly means quite, somewhat

explanation.surface: A note that repays someone fairly.
explanation.definitionFit: To requite is to repay a kindness or a wrong in kind, giving back what is fitting.

clue.text: Ready to perform — quiet, please!

parts.note: to do is to perform an act
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A performer is ready to go on, and the audience is asked for quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' here is British slang 'the ready', meaning cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosh and 'the ready' are both British slang words for money.

clue.text: Said to show indignation as new partner in union

indicators.note: said tells us the word is judged by its sound when spoken

parts.note: to bridle is to bristle with offence, raising the head like a reined horse

explanation.surface: A newly married partner is reported to be indignant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal describes things relating to a bride, the new partner in a marriage.

clue.text: A friend writing for entities formed initially, one can say

definitions.text: entities formed initially, one can say

parts.note: a crony is a close friend
MS is a manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A friend writes about things formed from initials.
explanation.walkthrough: These are words formed from initial letters and pronounced as words, like NATO.
explanation.definitionFit: Acronyms are words built from initials that can be spoken as words.

clue.text: Monarch joining society mostly misrepresented as exclusive

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown wrongly, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word society is kept

explanation.surface: A monarch joins a society that is misrepresented as an exclusive club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SOCIETY to SOCIET; with ER that gives ERSOCIET, which 'misrepresented' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is for a select inner circle only, so it is exclusive.

clue.text: It is offered and left in church

indicators.note: in tells us the joined words sit inside the abbreviation for the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Something is offered up and then left behind in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Votive candles are lit and offered by worshippers, so the short definition 'It is offered' leans on the church setting of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle is commonly offered as a votive light by worshippers.

clue.text: What swimmers do between laps is critical

definitions.meaning: in a pool, a swimmer touches the wall at the end of a length and goes off again
critical here means precarious, with the outcome in doubt

explanation.definitionFit: A risky, uncertain situation is called touch-and-go, and racing swimmers literally touch the end then go back.

clue.text: Lake, in general, is found in valley

indicators.note: in says the letter for lake is put inside the short form of general

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A lake is generally found in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' reads as 'usually', but GEN is general shortened and L goes in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Helping friend in sensible fashion

parts.note: a helping is a portion, or ration, of food
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Helping a friend is the sensible thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something rationally means doing it with reason, sensibly.

clue.text: Excel strategically, twice reversing in particular?

parts.note: in is replaced by its opposite, out
particular is replaced by its opposite, general

explanation.surface: To win by strategy, reverse yourself twice on a detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice reversing' tells you to swap each word of 'in particular' for its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: To outgeneral an opponent is to beat them through superior tactics.

clue.text: The third letter after Q

parts.note: the letter after Q is R, and the third of the three Rs of basic schooling is the one with sums

explanation.definitionFit: The three Rs are reading, writing and the subject of sums, which comes third.

clue.text: Rescue from tight spot, having trouble in fight

indicators.note: in says the word for trouble goes inside the word for a fight

parts.note: a bout is a boxing fight
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Someone in trouble during a fight needs rescuing from a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To bail out is to rescue a person or firm from difficulty, often financially.

clue.text: Raised objection to macho guy grabbing one artistic type

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: OB is a dictionary abbreviation for objection

indicators.note: grabbing says the macho man takes the numeral inside

parts.note: a he-man is a macho, muscular man
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone objected to a macho man grabbing an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A bohemian is an unconventional, artistic person.

clue.text: Present for your paper, occasionally

parts.note: present means at a place, here
this puzzle appeared in The Times, the reader's own newspaper

explanation.surface: A gift for your newspaper now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift, but it is AT as in being present at something.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at times happens occasionally, now and then.

clue.text: Always protecting one old fashioned sinner

indicators.note: protecting means the word for always wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: ever means always
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned sinner is always protected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' reshapes the three letters of 'old' before they and the one go inside; 'old fashioned' reads as a single description of the sinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An evildoer is someone who does wrong, a sinner.

clue.text: Observed sea mist covering cutter

indicators.note: covering in a down clue puts the sea mist on top of the other word

parts.note: a fret is a sea mist on the coast of England
saw means observed

explanation.surface: Someone saw a sea mist covering a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutter' seems to be a boat; it is a fine saw for curves.
explanation.definitionFit: A fretsaw is a fine-bladed saw for cutting intricate curves.

clue.text: Sort of shore bird, initially, as favourite topic

indicators.note: initially tells us the bird comes at the start, before the rearranged letters

parts.note: the hobby is a small falcon

indicators.note: sort of hints at a version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some kind of shore bird is someone's favourite topic of conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' reshuffles the five letters of 'shore'; 'initially' places the bird first. The hobby is a falcon, not a shore bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby horse is a pet subject someone keeps returning to.

clue.text: Shelter from hazard

definitions.meaning: on a golf course, a sand trap is a hazard

explanation.definitionFit: A bunker is both an underground refuge and a sand-filled golf hazard.

clue.text: Person who succeeds repeatedly in Scottish town atmosphere, say

indicators.note: say tells us the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: Ayr is a Scottish town and air is atmosphere; both are pronounced the same

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps succeeding in a Scottish town's atmosphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' signals that the one sound does double duty: AYR, a town on Scotland's west coast, and AIR both sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir succeeds to a title or estate when its holder dies.

clue.text: Art M. Monet composed, about right for artistic area

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the letter for right
composed means put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: The painter Monet composed a work, with the area full of artists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges ARTMMONET, and 'about' wraps that round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Montmartre is the Paris hill district famed for its painters' studios.

clue.text: Market-place displacing old heart in Eastern city

annotationWithheld.why: Market-place displacing old heart in Eastern city: AGORA less O (old, its heart) gives AGRA, but every legal form is refused: [old heart]O trips selectorAsCut, and [old]O is normalised into bare O under 'displacing', which trips delAsMove
annotationWithheld.clue: Market-place displacing old heart in Eastern city

clue.text: In earlier fashion, daughter covered the same ground

parts.note: retro styles imitate fashions of the past

explanation.surface: A daughter dressed in old styles walked the same route again.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrod is the past tense of retread, to walk over ground again.

clue.text: A very English mass, with vocal music and prayer

parts.note: M is the physics symbol for mass
an aria is a solo song in an opera

explanation.surface: A very English church mass, with singing and prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' suggests a church service; here it is just M.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ave Maria, or Hail Mary, is a Catholic prayer to the Virgin.

clue.text: Dark horse, unbroken and eccentric

parts.note: an unbroken horse has never been tamed, so it is wild
a card is an old word for an eccentric character

explanation.surface: An outsider horse that is untamed and odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a wild card and a dark horse are unknown competitors who may surprise everyone.
